audit.why: 51.06% over 705 games — marginally Ambessa's, decided by whether she closes before two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Jax four stages and Ambessa none on a matchup she wins, and contradicted the prose at three points: whys[2] calls level 3 'your real window', whys[4] says the level 6 all-in 'kills', and whys[5] calls first item 'your last clean favor window'. Levels 4-5 were marked Skill where whys[3] says 'he owns the window'.
audit.why: This lane is a race. Ambessa owns level 3, level 6 and the Eclipse spike; Jax owns level 2, the 4-5 gap and everything past two items once Grandmaster-at-Arms and armour items are up.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Jax / Ambessa / Jax / Ambessa / Ambessa / Jax in both layers — 3-3-1, which fits 51.06% and reads as the alternating race the prose describes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' in three places. Riot's current name is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Ambessa's level 6 spike is credited to 'R's flat armor pen plus heal-on-ability-damage', neither of which is in Riot's text for any of her abilities.
audit.why: A wrong ultimate name is the exact class of error this audit exists to catch, and it appears in the two-item spike, the last why and a wants.foe line. Grandmaster-at-Arms is also more than resists: every third consecutive attack deals bonus magic damage, which is why his attack-speed ramp matters against an armour-stacking Ambessa.
audit.corrected: All three renamed to Grandmaster-at-Arms, with the third-attack magic damage stated. Ambessa's 6 re-anchored on the 1250-unit blink and 110s-versus-130s ultimate race.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is described as if it blanks your whole commit — 'he dodges every one', 'your follow-up autos get dodged'. Riot's text is narrower and far more useful: 'dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies'. It dodges basic attacks. Ambessa's abilities land through it.
audit.why: This is the single piece of information that changes how the fight is played. Cunning Sweep, Sundering Slam, Lacerate, Repudiation and Public Execution all connect while Counter Strike is active — only the Medarda-empowered auto is wasted. So the correct sequencing is to dump abilities into the dodge window and hold the empowered auto until the counterattack has fired, rather than backing off entirely. The page's version tells you to disengage from a window you can actually spend most of your kit in.
audit.corrected: Stated in early, mid, spikes[1].text, whys[4], wants.you[1] and the interactions line, with Counter Strike's 17/15/13/11/9s cooldown attached so 'bait it' becomes countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page pairs 'Leap Strike-Empower' as one burst on one timer and never gives either cooldown.
audit.why: They are very different timers. Empower is 30 mana on 7/6/5/4/3s — effectively always available, and at rank 5 it is up every other trade. Leap Strike is 50 mana on 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s at 700 range. Counter Strike at 17s rank 1 is the only real window, and it is nearly twice as long as anything else he has.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added to whys[1], early, mid and breakdown.cooldowns, with the short trade keyed to a spent Counter Strike rather than to a spent Empower.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait it out first' has no number attached anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Counter Strike's 17-second rank-1 cooldown is the longest non-ultimate cooldown in the matchup and the only one worth building a plan around. Once it drops to 9 seconds at rank 5, baiting it stops being a reliable plan, which is part of why the lane slips away late.
audit.corrected: 17/15/13/11/9s stated in mid, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t, with the note that the window shrinks as he ranks it.

audit.why: The win condition — close before two items, then split rather than solo him — matches a 10/10 carry threat and Jax's resist-stacking ultimate. Left in place.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even and you have no combo yet — don't throw a lone Q into his range, since one ability and your empowered auto don't beat his Leap Strike-Empower burst. The early game lives and dies on his E: if you E-in and try to stack empowered autos into a raised Counter Strike, he dodges every one and stuns you. At 3 your real window opens — land Q to unlock Sundering Slam, drop E for the heavy slow, weave one or two empowered autos in a SHORT trade, then back off before his Q-W cooldowns reset.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even and you have no combo yet — don't throw a lone Q into his 700-range Leap Strike, since one ability and an empowered auto lose to it plus Empower. The early game lives on his E: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks for its duration, so your empowered autos vanish into it while every ability you cast still lands. At 3 your window opens — land Q to unlock Sundering Slam, drop E for the slow, and take a SHORT trade once his 17s E is spent.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your weakest patch — your cooldowns are longest while his Leap Strike-Empower stays online, so farm and don't force a trade you'll lose. Six flips it: Public Execution blinks you behind him, suppresses, and your R's flat armor pen plus heal-on-ability-damage makes a committed all-in lethal. The trap is still Counter Strike — if it's up when you blink in, your follow-up autos get dodged and you eat the stun. Bait it out first (force it on a Q poke or a fake step-up), THEN R while it's on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your weakest patch — your cooldowns are longest while Empower refreshes every 5 seconds for 30 mana, so farm and don’t force a trade you’ll lose. Six flips it: Public Execution blinks 1250 units, suppresses him and slams him down stunned, and that chain beats a 700-range leap. The trap is Counter Strike, 17s at rank 1: if it is raised when you land, pour abilities into it — they connect — and hold the empowered auto until the counterattack has fired, then finish him.

edits.before: Your first-item Eclipse spike with the Q max is your last clean favor window — Q1-auto-Q2 chunks him before Trinity Force comes fully online, so end the lane there. After that he reclaims the duel: Grandmaster's Might stacks bonus armor and MR, Steelcaps plus an armor item wall your physical burst, and Counter Strike still erases your empowered-auto window. Don't run it down into a two-item Jax — split, take towers, and save your R for picks in skirmishes instead of soloing him.
edits.after: Your first-item Eclipse spike with the Q max is your last clean favor window — the rank-5 Q returns in 10s, so Q1-auto-Q2 chunks him before Trinity Force lands. After that he reclaims the duel: his ultimate adds armour and MR and makes every third consecutive attack deal bonus magic damage, Steelcaps walls your physical burst, and Counter Strike is down to a 9-second cooldown. Don’t solo a two-item Jax — split, take towers, and save R for picks.

notes: The flagged wrong name was real: Jax's ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms, and the page called it 'Grandmaster's Might' — an old name — in three separate fields. The packet's suspectNames flagged 'Counter Strike's' and 'Leap Strike-' instead, both of which are correct names, so the near-miss detector missed the actual error sitting in the same sentence. The Counter Strike scope error is the bigger practical fix: Riot's text says it dodges incoming ATTACKS, so Ambessa's five abilities all connect through it and only the Medarda-empowered auto is wasted, which turns 'disengage' into 'keep casting, hold the hit'. Unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'R's flat armor pen' and 'heal-on-ability-damage' — the same phantom passive that appears across this champion's whole matchup set. One thing I could not settle and did not assert: whether Counter Strike's dodge also applies to the on-hit portion of a Medarda-empowered attack versus the attack as a whole, and whether Public Execution's suppression can be applied while Counter Strike is already active. BLOCKER worth the user’s attention: I could not actually write Jax’s correct ultimate name into the data. tools/apply-proposals.js rejects any  matching / (...|challenger|grandmaster|...) /i as “mentions an elo tier”, and “Grandmaster-at-Arms” contains the word grandmaster. The same filter also rejects the existing wrong name “Grandmaster’s Might”, which is very likely why that error has survived: every correction to it is silently dropped. I worked around it by describing the ultimate precisely without naming it (“his ultimate adds armour and MR and makes every third consecutive attack deal bonus magic damage”), which removes the wrong name without tripping the filter, but the ability still ends up unnamed on the page. The ELO regex needs a negative lookahead for “grandmaster-at-arms”, or a whitelist of ability names, before any Jax matchup in any lane can name his R correctly.
